original_question: Is it consistent that the splitting number s equals ℵ1 and nevertheless the strong polarized relation \( inom{s}{\omega} 	o  inom{s}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds, meaning every 2-coloring of s×ω has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A| = s and |B| = ω?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.2 of the arXiv version (renumbered as Section 3, Problem 3.2 in the published version).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's exact target very closely: it asks for the consistency of 𝔰 = ℵ1 together with the positive strong polarized relation for the pair (𝔰, ω), and it correctly expands the partition notation as a monochromatic rectangle of sizes 𝔰 and ω for every 2-coloring.
missing_details: State explicitly that the question is about consistency with ZFC, i.e. the existence of a model or forcing extension satisfying the stated properties.
Use the standard symbol 𝔰 and say explicitly that it denotes the splitting number.
Specify that the witnesses are sets A ⊆ 𝔰 and B ⊆ ω.
Use the paper's exact formulation that the coloring is constant on A × B, which is the meaning of the strong polarized notation in Definition 0.1.
Keep the scope strictly to 𝔰 = ℵ1; do not import the separate neighboring variants involving 𝔲 = 𝔰 or 𝔰 < 𝔠, which the paper lists as different problems.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that the splitting number 𝔰 equals ℵ1 and nevertheless the strong polarized partition relation \binom{𝔰}{\omega} \rightarrow \binom{𝔰}{\omega}^{1,1}_2 holds; that is, for every coloring c: 𝔰 × ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ 𝔰 and B ⊆ ω with |A| = 𝔰 and |B| = ω such that c restricted to A × B is constant?
justification: This is essentially the paper's exact question. Definition 0.1 gives the formal meaning of the strong polarized notation. Theorem 1.6 supplies the nearby background that positive relations hold below the splitting number, which explains why the authors then focus on 𝔰 itself. In Section 2 they state verbatim the countable-case problem asking whether it is consistent that 𝔰 = ℵ1 yet \binom{𝔰}{\omega} \rightarrow \binom{𝔰}{\omega}^{1,1}_2. The nearby Problem 2.4 is a different variant because it adds the extra hypothesis 𝔰 = 𝔲, so your draft should be aligned with Problem 2.2 and not broadened.
